$comment: The job this repository EXPECTS to carry a required status context, and what that job
must be performing for the expectation to mean anything.
Why a checked-in file at all: which checks branch protection actually requires is a
repository setting, and a pull request cannot read it. So the expectation is declared
here and the workflow hygiene lane checks the tree against this file. Reading live
settings is forbidden, because a check that cannot run on a pull request blocks nothing.
This file states an expectation. It cannot prove the setting agrees with it. What it can
do — and what the lane does — is make a change that would invalidate the expectation fail
IF THE SETTING IS CHANGED TO MATCH THIS FILE, the required context must be `ci-pass` and
not `build`. That is the point of the entry below, and it is a repository-settings change

why: `ci-pass` and not `build`, which is where this pointed until review finding [28] on
PR #794 measured what that cost: `build` declares no `needs` at all, so requiring it
and nothing else means every Vitest lane, `lint` and `check-types`
can fail while the merge condition is satisfied. The one job whose
result depends on theirs is the aggregate verdict, so that is the one worth requiring.
The earlier entry argued the opposite from a real constraint: the verdict carries
`if: always()`, and the hygiene lane's property 2 rejected any condition on a declared
job, because a skipped job reports SUCCESS to branch protection. That approximation is
right for every condition except this one — `always()` is what guarantees the job
runs. The lane now says so, and a condition that is not `always()` is still fatal.
Its dependencies DO carry conditions (`check-types`, `test` and the rest run on
`needs.detect.outputs.full`), and that is the arrangement rather than a hole: the
verdict is derived by iterating the serialized `needs` map, and its accepting set
includes `skipped`. A documentation-only pull request skips those lanes, the verdict
runs anyway and passes; a failing lane makes it fail. Neither is reachable while the
context sits on a job that never looks at them.
The executed-instance figure in the spec is written as 'at most 5 executed instances,
4 once the job named `build` may carry a condition'. The fourth is not yet realised:
`build` still carries no condition, so it still runs on a documentation-only pull
request, and making it conditional is a separate change with its own measurement.
The fifth instance is the lane that runs the agent-integration mirror guards, which
took a runner of its own and which lane selection may never skip.
dependenciesNote: The EXACT set of jobs the aggregate depends on, and the reason it is pinned here rather
than left to the workflow: `${{ toJSON(needs) }}` contains only the jobs still listed in
`needs:`, so deleting a name from that list removes a whole lane from the verdict while
the lane keeps running and keeps failing. Review finding [80] measured the consequence —
`lint`, `check-types` and `test` all deleted, all still red, and the
required context green, with the topology test that would notice sitting inside the very
`test` job that had been removed from the aggregate.
Equality, in both directions. A missing name is the attack; an EXTRA name is a lane whose
result now gates the merge and whose addition nobody declared, and the discipline in this
file is that a change to what the required context means is a change a reviewer reads.
Adding a lane is two edits on purpose.
unconditionalDependenciesNote: These jobs host the lint lanes that run on every pull request.
Each must remain in needs, carry no condition, and stay absent from dependencyConditions.
The topology test independently resolves every exempt lane to its host and checks this list.

includes `skipped`, because a documentation-only pull request legitimately runs none of
these lanes — so the skip decision is load-bearing, and every part of it has to be pinned

or the acceptance of `skipped` becomes the hole.
A job listed here must carry that condition verbatim. A job NOT listed must carry no
condition at all. Review finding [81]: `if: false` on `test`, or any narrowing of the
expression, skips the lane, the verdict accepts the skip, and nothing else in the tree
`detect`, `lint`, `mirror-surface` and `build` are deliberately absent, which is the assertion
that they run on every pull request. `mirror-surface` cannot be skipped because the surface it
checks — the rule mirror, the skill links, the reviewer vocabulary — is what a change to those
documents breaks, and such a change is exactly the one a detection-derived condition would
route past it. `BR-0015-0011` binds that on review: a lane moved into a job of its own gains
neither a condition nor an entry above.
dependencyMatricesNote: The matrix values a gated lane expands over, pinned exactly.
Review finding [97]: `Run tests (${{ matrix.slice }})` is digested with the EXPRESSION in it,
so the digest says nothing about what the expression expands to. Replacing a value with
`unit || true #` hands the shell `pnpm -C packages/qfai test:unit || true #`, which succeeds
whatever the tests did — and removing values from the list drops whole slices — while the
pinned body and every other property stay exactly as they were.
Equality, in both directions and in order. A dropped value is a slice that stopped running; an
added one is a leg whose check name branch protection has never seen; and a REWRITTEN one is
shell the digest cannot see. This is the same obligation `verificationBodies` carries for a
step's text, applied to the other half of what the step actually runs.
TWO lanes are sliced now, and each is pinned separately. `node-floor` runs the same seven
slices, so a value rewritten in its list reaches its shell exactly as one rewritten in the
`test` job's reaches that one — and a value dropped from it stops a slice being exercised on
the engines floor while the `test` job still runs it and the lane still reports green. That
the two lists are identical is the point and not a reason to share one entry: they are two
declarations in the workflow, so they are two declarations here.
gateOutputsNote: The wiring the conditions above read, pinned expression by expression. Review finding
[81]: rewiring `detect.outputs.full` to `${{ false }}` — or to a step output that does not
exist — skips every gated lane without touching a single condition or a single line of the
classifier, and `skipped` is accepting. The classifier's own tests are in `test`, which is
one of the lanes that skips.
Equality again, and one more property the lane checks: an expression of the form
`${{ steps.<id>.outputs.<name> }}` must name a step that job actually declares with that
`id`. A mapping that reads a step nobody defines is a mapping that always answers empty,
which is the same skip by a quieter route.
The classifier's BODY is pinned separately, by its membership in `verificationSet` and its
digest in `verificationBodies`: the wiring and the program are two edits and both are read.
That claim was FALSE when it was written, and an audit of this file found it: the classifier
step was in neither list, so the wiring was pinned and the program behind it was not. Two
literal edits inside its heredoc — `emit(false, 'docs-only')` — skipped five of the eight lanes
into an accepting `skipped`, including the lane whose tests execute that very heredoc. It is a
member of `verificationSet` now, and `detect` carries no condition, so it belongs to the

The lane checks three things: the file holds what this declares, the tree hashes to what the

An allow-list rather than a ban, because the closure legitimately needs two: the checkout every

Review finding [88]: the scan that reads a local action's steps followed `./` references only,
so `uses: attacker/action@<sha>` inside `.github/actions/setup` was passed over without a

An allow-list rather than a ban, because the preamble legitimately needs one: `setup-node` is

Steps in the WORKFLOWS themselves are not governed here: those references sit in the diff a

preflight.step: Verify the toolchain action before running it

preflightNote: The step that must run before any local composite action does, and the job it runs in.
Review finding [82]: `lint` invokes `./.github/actions/setup` before it runs any guard, and a
pull request can edit that action. A step at the top of it appending `BASH_ENV=<a script that
exits 0>` to the environment file makes every later `shell: bash` step exit 0 without running
its body — the hygiene lane among them. The lane reports that write and cannot report it in
that scenario, because it is one of the steps that never runs.
So the refusal is moved ahead of the action, and this entry is what keeps it there. The lane
checks three things: the named job declares the named step; every step before it carries
neither `run:` nor a local `uses:`, so nothing can have set an environment file first; and the
step is in `verificationSet`, so its body is pinned like every other required verification.
`mayPrecede` is the closed set of `uses:` references allowed AHEAD of it. Review finding [94]:
the order check treated `run:` and local `uses:` as work and everything else as inert, so
`uses: attacker/action@<sha>` could sit before the refusal — `action-pin` proves such a
reference is immutable and says nothing about what it does. An external action ahead of the
pre-flight can write a workflow command file, or replace the very script the pre-flight is
about to run, out of the checkout it produced.
`actions/checkout` is on it because the pre-flight has to read this repository's files to
refuse anything, and pinned to the SHA for the same reason every other reference here is.

reviewer of a diff notices moving. The lane accepts an item performed by the declared
job OR by a job it depends on, so relocating work into a dependency is legal and
relocating it out of reach is not.
The six build-side items are unchanged from when this entry named `build`: `build` is
inside `ci-pass`'s `needs`, so they remain in reach and are still enumerated. The
verdict's own step joins them, because the property this context carries is that the
verdict was actually derived rather than that the job merely existed.
The optional report upload is deliberately absent: it ends in a tolerated failure and
cannot fail the job, so it is not a verification however it is named.
gatedVerificationsNote: The work of the lanes that are ALLOWED to skip, pinned by body without being required to run.
A lane held only as a declared dependency, by name and condition, can have its `run` replaced
with `true`: the hygiene lane stays silent, the job green and `ci-pass` green, while the work
the lane existed for stops being done at all. Being IN the aggregate is not the same claim as
Separate from `verificationSet` because the property is different, not because the obligation
is weaker. A `verificationSet` item must be performed UNCONDITIONALLY, and these four sit in
jobs that carry `needs.detect.outputs.full` — which is the arrangement rather than a hole: a
documentation-only pull request legitimately runs none of them, and the verdict accepts the
skip. What must not change without a reviewer reading it is WHAT THEY DO when they run.
So the lane checks each one's body digest against `verificationBodies`, requires the step to
carry no condition and no `continue-on-error` of its own — the JOB's declared condition is the
only one allowed, and it is pinned in `dependencyConditions` — and requires every step sharing
the name to agree, for the reason `verificationBodiesNote` gives: a name is not a step.
`Run lint gate` is NOT here. `lint` carries no condition, so `pnpm ci:lint` is an ordinary
unconditional verification and joins `verificationSet` with the rest.
verificationBodiesNote: A digest of each verification step's `run` / `uses` / `with` / `env`, and of the package
scripts that `run` invokes — what the step DOES, with its name deliberately excluded so
the pin cannot agree with itself.

documentationOnlyCostPinNote: What a documentation-only pull request costs, pinned as the jobs it executes and the sum of
their declared `timeout-minutes`.
A job executes on that path when nothing can prevent it: no condition at all, or a condition
whose whole expression is `always()`. The aggregate verdict is in the set for that second
reason — `always()` is what makes it run when its needs are skipped, which is this path.
The unit is runner-minutes rather than job instances. Instances charges +1 for a change that
shortens the run and adds no work, and the measure this replaced was a set equality over four
job names, which refused exactly such a change.
This is NOT a cost bound, and the distinction is load-bearing. Enforcement is equality against
a value recomputed from the same tree, so a clause forbidding a higher cost could not fail:
once the pinner has run, no state of the tree violates it. What the pin refuses is a change
that did not re-pin — which is what makes a raise deliberate and puts the new figure in a diff.
Whether the figure is acceptable is a cost claim, and a cost claim arrives with measured
before-and-after numbers rather than on argument.
`timeout-minutes` is the declared worst case, not a measurement, so the sum sits far above what
the path really costs. It still catches a runaway job and a forgotten raise, which is the class
a declared ceiling can catch.
Re-pinned by `node scripts/pin-documentation-only-cost.mjs`, which imports the lane's own
computation rather than restating it. `dependencies` and `dependencyConditions` above carry the
membership half of the same rule, scoped to the jobs this context depends on — a narrower set,
because the verdict executes and is not one of its own dependencies.
codePathCostPinNote: What a code-path pull request costs, pinned as four figures recomputed from the workflow tree.
Every job runs on that path, so the cost is a property of the tree rather than of a condition.
`instances` is a job's matrix legs summed over the tree — what a check-name list and a bill both
count. `timeoutMinutesSum` is the declared ceiling per instance summed the same way.
`installInstances` is the instances that run the toolchain action, one frozen-lockfile install
each.
`buildJobs` names JOBS and not instances, and that is a limit stated rather than hidden. Two of
the three condition their build step on the matrix leg, so an instance figure would need
`matrix.slice == 'e2e' || matrix.slice == 'integration'` evaluated, and this lane evaluates no
GitHub expression. The jobs figure still moves when a build is added to or removed from a job,
which is the change a pin has to catch.
This is NOT a cost bound. Enforcement is equality against a value derived from the same tree, so
a clause forbidding a higher cost could not fail: once the pinner has run, no state of the tree
violates it. What the pin refuses is a change that did not re-pin — which is what makes a raise
deliberate and puts the new figure in a diff. Whether the figure is acceptable is a cost claim,
and a cost claim arrives with measured before-and-after numbers rather than on argument.
Nor does it compare the pin with a RUN. Nothing here reads what a run actually cost: that needs
the forge's API and a finished run, which no lint lane has. A tree that was always more
expensive than it declared is therefore outside this rule, and that gap is deliberate.
`timeout-minutes` is the declared worst case, so the sum sits far above what the path really
costs. It still catches a runaway job and a forgotten raise, which is the class a declared
ceiling can catch.
